title: C-Style Strings and Null Terminators
learningObjectives: Explain c-style strings and null terminators.
Describe relevant storage, indexing and size rules.
Trace a collection operation or traversal.
Recognize bounds, lifetime or input pitfalls.
Apply the type to a practical collection task.

understand.concept: C-style strings are character arrays ending with '\0'. C-string routines rely on a valid terminator.
understand.whyItMatters: Low-level interfaces and legacy code use null-terminated text.
understand.explain: Allocate room for the terminator and prevent buffer overflows.

examples.title: Null-terminated buffer
examples.explanation: The null character marks the end of a C string.

examples.title: Literal array
examples.code: char word[]="cat";\n// c, a, t and '\\0'

examples.title: C-string length
examples.explanation: strlen excludes the null terminator; include cstring.

examples.title: Buffer capacity
examples.code: char buffer[5]{};\n// up to 4 text characters plus '\\0'
examples.explanation: Capacity must include the terminator slot.

examples.title: Explicit termination
examples.explanation: The explicit terminator makes a valid C string.

practise.guidedTask: Trace all five C-Style Strings and Null Terminators examples. Record sizes, indexes, values and condition checks. Identify first/last valid element and relevant edge cases.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ data-processing program demonstrating c-style strings and null terminators. Test typical values, empty/boundary cases, and invalid input or indexing where relevant. Explain why this collection is appropriate.
hints: Use zero-based indexes and verify bounds.
Prefer range-based traversal when index is unnecessary.
Check emptiness before operations such as front or pop_back.
Test first, last and invalid boundaries.

questions.explanation: C-string functions search for a terminator.
